articles.title: Democrats take control of US Congress in major rebuke of Trump. What comes next?
articles.author: Devin B. Martinez
articles.content_excerpt: Democrats won control of the United States Congress in the country’s midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3, in a crushing rebuke of US President Donald Trump’s second term. The Republicans lost at least seven Senate seats in states that have traditionally been strongholds for the right-wing party. The party also lost over two dozen House districts to the Democrats. In the 2024 presidential election, Trump had won some of these districts by double-digit percentage points. Kansas will have a Democratic senator for the first time in nearly a century. North and South Carolina and even Texas have flipped to the Democrats in an unprecedented shift for those states. articles.title: “Over a Decade of Organizing”: Keisha Lance Bottoms Elected First Black Woman Governor in U.S. History
articles.content_excerpt: Image Credit: KeishaForGA/Facebook Black voters in Georgia on Tuesday said, “Not today, Satan,” according to professor Carol Anderson, professor of African American studies at Emory University. Despite the Trump administration’s efforts to disenfranchise Black voters in the South this election cycle and the Supreme Court’s gutting of the Voting Rights Act, she says there was “massive turnout” that propelled Democrats to victory. Former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated billionaire Republican healthcare executive Rick Jackson, becoming the first Black woman ever elected governor in the United States. Incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff also handily won his bid for reelection. Please check back later for full transcript.

articles.title: Protest near Kyiv exposes detention of AWOL soldiers
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: On Monday, November 2, protesters gathered in Petropavlivska Borshchahivka in the Kyiv region, outside a building that was used as a detention site holding soldiers absent without leave and recruits. Facing army and police forces, alongside non-uniformed attackers, protesters were able to bring out the men held inside. Many of the men who left the building displayed signs of physical violence. Four men – confirmed to be soldiers absent without leave – were hospitalized, while videos from the ground testimonies showed others as battered and bruised. The detention site was associated with the Azov Corps of the National Guard of Ukraine. articles.title: UN mission on Western Sahara lapses after vote deadlock in security council
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: The United Nations Security Council failed to reach an agreement on the future of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) following a contentious meeting on October 30, leaving the mission without a renewed mandate for the first time since its establishment in 1991. The meeting saw Russia veto a United States-sponsored draft resolution that had received 11 votes in favor, one against, and three abstentions. The proposed resolution sought to renew the mission’s mandate for another year while making significant changes to its name, structure and political framework, including making Morocco’s autonomy proposal the basis for negotiations over the territory. articles.title: Thousands join protests in New Delhi denouncing electoral manipulation
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Hundreds of thousands took to India’s capital, New Delhi, on Sunday, November 1, to demand the sacking of the country’s Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) over allegations of manipulation and rigging various elections in India. The protesters marched in smaller groups from different corners of the city in the early morning finally converging at the central Ramlila Maidan under the call to “save democracy” made by the main block of opposition parties called the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance, or INDIA. articles.title: Israeli forces withdraw from Hebron following 11-day large-scale operation
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: The Israeli forces withdrew from the West Bank southern city of Hebron on Monday, November 2, after carrying out an extensive military operation that saw the displacement of hundreds of families and massive destruction of residential buildings over the span of 11 days. The operation, which included a full lockdown of the West Bank and was considered by many as a collective punishment of the entire Palestinian population in the occupied territory, was launched on October 23, after two Israeli soldiers were shot dead by two Palestinian men near a military checkpoint in the Farsh al-Hawa area. According to Hebron Municipality, 15 homes and facilities were demolished in the assault, while 327 shops were closed, with direct daily economic losses estimated at roughly $3.8 million.
